ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), SC 2000, c 17; Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, ss 462.31 and 83.03; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Law), SC 2017, c 21; Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c 57, Part 2, including the unlimited liability company provisions; Beneficial Ownership Transparency Act, SBC 2020, c 15, as amended.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization as applicable under the origin jurisdiction's authentication regime

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary / board of directors of the UBO, attested by a notary public

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille not required for internal BC registry maintenance; if the declaration is to be used abroad, Global Affairs Canada or the applicable provincial competent authority may issue an apostille

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-transaction and continuous screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, and authorized signatories against FINTRAC PEP categories under SOR/2002-184 (foreign PEP, domestic PEP, and heads of international organizations), the OFAC SDN list, the UN Consolidated Security Council Sanctions List, and Global Affairs Canada lists under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Law). Procedures include government-issued photo identification, corporate flow-through verification to natural persons, beneficial ownership accounting at the 25% ownership/control threshold, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification for PEPs, adverse media review, annual re-certification of the ISC register, and ongoing transaction monitoring through the Stripe and Apple IAP payment rails.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Registries and Online Services (Corporate Online), https://www.bcregistry.gov.bc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory corporate names must be expressed in Roman/Latin characters. Non-English and non-French names must be transliterated or translated into a Roman-script form, and a certified translation or notarized declaration will support the transliteration. The legal element of a BC unlimited liability company must be 'ULC' or 'Unlimited Liability Company'; the name must not carry limited-liability markers such as 'Limited', 'Ltd.', 'Incorporated', or 'Inc.'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon refusal, the BC Registrar issues a written refusal notice. The applicant may re-file a new name reservation with a revised name through Corporate Online, or, within 21 days of the refusal notice, bring an application for review or appeal to the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the applicable appeal provision of the Business Corporations Act. An existing 56-day name reservation may be renewed for two further 56-day periods by filing a renewal before expiry, provided no refusal or conflicting reservation is on record.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for this low-risk cloud software application if the virtual office provider maintains a physical street address in British Columbia, accepts legal process and government notices during business hours, and is not a post-office box or drop box. The virtual address satisfies the BC registered-office requirement under the Business Corporations Act, but it does not alone evidence Canadian commercial substance or CRA tax-residency substance; actual employees, business records, board decision-making, and bank accounts should be weighed separately for CRA and treaty purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: estimated 3% annual probability of an unannounced BC Registrar verification of the registered-office consent and quasi-physical presence, and approximately 8% cumulative risk of an on-site CRA records audit during the first three fiscal years for a non-resident-owned ULC in an unlicensed fintech-software profile. The product uses no cash or securities custody, and the AML risk tier is Low_Risk_Standard.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (British Columbia), SBC 2002, c. 57, as amended, including Part 2 (Incorporation), the Notice of Articles regime, and the Act's provisions governing unlimited liability companies, registered offices and records offices.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: British Columbia Registrar of Companies / BC Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance, Victoria, British Columbia.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Articles (Form 1), together with optional Articles and the Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: British Columbia imposes no statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow capital requirement. The ULC may be incorporated with nominal issued share capital; shareholders of an unlimited liability company remain jointly and severally liable for the company's debts to the extent provided under applicable corporate law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the Company's incorporation as an unlimited liability company under the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia) is acknowledged and ratified. FURTHER RESOLVED that the share subscriptions of the founding shareholders are approved and the directors shall issue the subscribed shares for lawful consideration. FURTHER RESOLVED that the registered office and records office named in the Notice of Articles are confirmed as the Company's statutory offices. FURTHER RESOLVED that the individuals listed in the officer schedule are appointed as President, Secretary and Chief Financial Officer, each to serve until replaced. FURTHER RESOLVED that the corporate seal, bank signatories and tax filings are authorized. This resolution is effective upon certification by the Corporate Secretary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registrar of Companies via BC Corporate Online / BC Registry Services.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If a distinctive name is desired, conduct a name screening search through BC Registry Services and submit a Name Reservation Request online. The corporate name must include the required ULC identifier such as 'ULC' or 'Unlimited Liability Company'. Alternatively, the incorporator may choose a numbered BC ULC, which avoids a name reservation. Notarization is not required for online requests; third-party filers must attach an executed agency authorization.
required_dossiers: Name Reservation Request (if using a custom name)
Executed agent authorization (optional, if filing through an agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused, submit a revised name reservation with a different distinctive element, or proceed as a numbered British Columbia ULC. A refusal does not prejudice later re-submission after correcting the identified conflict.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of incorporation agreement, notice of articles and articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registrar of Companies / Corporate Registry; document preparation by the incorporator or legal counsel.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Incorporation Agreement, Notice of Articles (Form 1), and, if the incorporators intend to opt out of the statutory default governance model, the Articles. The Notice of Articles must identify the ULC status, share structure, registered office and records office, and first directors. Each incorporator must execute the Incorporation Agreement. No notarization is required at the pre-filing stage; however, the executed originals must be retained in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Articles (if non-default governance provisions are adopted)
Consent to act as director from each first director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar identifies an incompleteness or inconsistency in the draft, amend and resubmit the affected document within the Registrar's requisition period. If the requisition period lapses, re-commence the filing with corrected documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory filing and issuance of certificate of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registrar of Companies / Corporate Registry, Victoria, British Columbia.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the completed Notice of Articles and any adopted Articles electronically through BC Corporate Online, or physically with the BC Corporate Registry, and pay the prescribed filing fee (currently CAD 350). The Registrar will issue a Certificate of Incorporation showing the effective date and time. The company exists from the date and time recorded on the certificate. Notarization is not required for the standard online filing; an agent filing under a power of attorney must have the power of attorney notarized if requested.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of the incorporation fee
Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the electronic filing is queried, read the Registrar's requisition, correct the specified data fields and re-submit through BC Corporate Online. If the requisition is not cured within the statutory deadline, the application may be deemed abandoned; a fresh application may be filed after all deficiencies are resolved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors of the Company; internal corporate act, no registry filing required except where changes are made to registered office or directors.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or execute a unanimous written consent of directors. The board must approve and ratify the incorporation, accept the share subscriptions, issue subscribed shares, confirm the registered office and records office, appoint officers, adopt the corporate seal, designate bank signatories, set the fiscal year end, and authorize initial tax filings. Minutes or written consents must be filed in the corporate minute book. Notarization is not required for internal corporate resolutions.
required_dossiers: First board resolution or unanimous written consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director fails to attend or sign, call a properly noticed board meeting to establish quorum. If directors are unable or unwilling to act, the shareholders may appoint replacement directors under the Articles and file the required notice of change with the Corporate Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, payroll and workers' compensation registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency Business Registration Online; WorkSafeBC; BC Ministry of Finance as applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the BC ULC with the Canada Revenue Agency to obtain a federal Business Number, and enroll for corporate tax, GST/HST, and payroll program accounts as required. If the company will have employees in British Columbia, register with WorkSafeBC under the Workers Compensation Act and with the BC Ministry of Finance for any applicable provincial tax accounts. Use the Certificate of Incorporation and the officer list from the first board resolution. Standard registrations do not require notarization; the CRA may request director identification in response to fraud prevention controls.
required_dossiers: First board resolution and officer appointment schedule
Business owner and director identification details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or WorkSafeBC queries the registration, submit the Certificate of Incorporation, Notice of Articles and director/officer identification. Correct any address or corporate details with the BC Corporate Registry and re-file the registration. Penalties resulting from registry-related identity adjustments may be abated on written request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal business licence, fire safety and occupational clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipal business licence office; local fire authority; WorkSafeBC; British Columbia Environmental Assessment Office where applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the company maintains a physical office or business premises, apply for a municipal business licence and any required occupancy permit. Arrange a fire safety inspection under the BC Fire Code and register with WorkSafeBC for occupational health and safety compliance. For a remote or cloud-based software business, a home-based business licence may be required. Complete the applicable environmental checklist; no full environmental impact assessment is required for office-based software operations. Notarization is required only where the municipality asks for a certified copy of a lease or statutory declaration.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or proof of premises ownership
Fire safety inspection report or certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal business licence, occupancy permit or fire clearance is refused, remedy the identified building or fire safety deficiencies and request a re-inspection. If a land-use variance is required, apply to the local property standards committee or appeal as provided by the applicable municipal bylaw. For a standard office software use, a full EIA classification will not apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Local municipal planning and business licensing department; WorkSafeBC; British Columbia Environmental Assessment Office under the Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business Licence for General Office / Cloud Software Services

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: British Columbia Environmental Assessment Office (Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / registration-level; the fintech software activity is not a designated reviewable project under Schedule 1 of the Environmental Assessment Act, SBC 2018, c. 51, and a full EIA is not required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial effluent, VOC or hazardous waste discharge thresholds apply to cloud software operations. The company must comply with municipal wastewater, solid waste, recycling and electronic waste bylaws under the Environmental Management Act and applicable provincial regulations. Any emergency backup generator must satisfy local air emission permitting limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Municipal occupancy permit and fire safety clearance under the BC Fire Code; WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety clearance; compliance with the Workers Compensation Act; office structural load and life-safety requirements are confirmed through the occupancy permit process; no high-hazard industrial or civil-defense permit applies to software and data-application activities.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada — corporate income tax and GST/HST registration, returns, and audit; portal: CRA My Business Account / Business Registration Online (BRO) at https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html. Provincial: British Columbia Ministry of Finance, Consumer Taxation Branch — BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST) registration, returns, and audit via eTaxBC at https://etax.gov.bc.ca. Company registry: BC Registrar of Companies through BC Corporate Online at https://www.bcregistry.gov.bc.ca.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Foreign investor incorporates the BC Unlimited Liability Company (ULC) under the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia) via BC Corporate Online; the registry issues a 9-digit BC incorporation number; no minimum capital is required and non-resident ownership is permitted. 2) The ULC applies to CRA for a 9-digit federal Business Number (BN) using Form RC1 'Request for a Business Number' or via BRO; add the 'RT' program account for GST/HST and the 'RC' account for payroll if staff are engaged. Non-resident applicants must attach certified articles/certificate of incorporation, identify the Canadian registered office and tax representative, and provide the foreign parent documentation; CRA mails the BN confirmation, which also serves as the corporate income tax account. 3) If the ULC supplies taxable software or services into British Columbia, register for BC PST via eTaxBC (except where BC taxable sales were CAD 10,000 or less in the trailing 12 months), obtaining a BC PST vendor number. 4) Maintain Canadian books and records, file the annual BC Registry Report, and file CRA T2 corporate returns with Schedule 50 where foreign ownership exceeds 25%.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible for U.S. federal tax purposes because a Canadian Unlimited Liability Company is not a per se corporation under Treas. Reg. §301.7701-2(b)(8); a single U.S. shareholder may treat the ULC as a disregarded entity and multiple U.S. shareholders as a partnership under check-the-box default rules. For Canadian federal and British Columbia income tax purposes the ULC is an entity-level taxable corporation resident in Canada (deemed resident under ITA s.250(4)(a)), with no statutory flow-through for Canadian tax and no territorial exemption — worldwide income is taxable and distributions may attract deemed-dividend treatment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: U.S. owners may make a check-the-box election (IRS Form 8832, effective date plus 75-day filing window) choosing disregarded entity/partnership/corporation status solely for U.S. federal tax; CRA is not bound by the U.S. election. Canadian law provides no check-the-box; a ULC remains a Canadian corporation. GST/HST planning election: ETA s.156 allows closely related corporations to elect that intercorporate supplies are made for nil consideration. Hybrid mismatch: Canada's draft hybrid arrangement rules (proposed ITA ss.18.2/18.3) disallow deductions for hybrid mismatches and contain no taxpayer election; OECD Action 2 planning should be documented in the master file.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the central monetary authority; however, Canada maintains no dedicated foreign-exchange control administration. The regulatory perimeter for cross-border treasury activity is jointly governed by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for prudential bank supervision, the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist-financing surveillance under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), and the Department of Finance Canada for sanctions and trade policy. No approval from the Bank of Canada is required for capital account transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full current-account and capital-account convertibility exists for the Canadian dollar, a freely floating G10 currency with no exchange-control approval, quota, surrender, or two-tier rate mechanism. Profit remittance is unrestricted by statute, subject only to Part XIII non-resident withholding tax under the Income Tax Act (Canada): 25% statutory rate on dividends, typically reduced to 5%–15% under Article X of the Canada–U.S. Tax Treaty. For a British Columbia ULC, particular attention is required for the deemed-dividend rule in subsection 84(2) of the Income Tax Act when share capital is reduced, shares are redeemed, or the corporation is wound up, because such distributions may be recharacterized as dividends. Cross-border electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more trigger FINTRAC EFT reporting obligations for the Canadian bank, not prior authorization by the state.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory timeline for repatriation of export or service proceeds, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no requirement to surrender foreign currency earned by a resident exporter. The ULC may freely maintain foreign-currency accounts in Canada or offshore, subject to ordinary AML due diligence, FATCA/CRS account disclosure, and, where aggregate specified foreign property exceeds CAD 100,000, Form T1135 information reporting under section 233.3 of the Income Tax Act.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium — offshore digital EMI-style platforms (Wise Business, Airwallex, Payoneer, or similar non-chartered payment institutions) are legally viable only as auxiliary payment and FX-settlement rails, not as the primary treasury bank. They are not authorized Canadian deposit-taking institutions under the Bank Act and cannot hold regulated capital-escrow funds or issue Canadian clearing-routing numbers. If they solicit Canadian clients, they must register as money services businesses with FINTRAC. The ULC itself must not be an MSB; given the target rails (Stripe and Apple IAP) and the Low_Risk_Standard AML classification, a written FINTRAC exemption assessment is recommended to demonstrate that the ULC only collects its own software revenue and does not transmit third-party funds.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No Canadian statute mandates a physical director appearance for corporate account opening, but prudential bank policy and PCMLTFA enhanced-due-diligence rules render it de facto necessary for first-time non-resident shareholders of a ULC. Schedule I banks standardly require either (i) an in-person interview with at least one authorized director or signatory at a Canadian branch, or (ii) a high-definition video interview with the bank's compliance officer supplemented by Canadian-counsel-notarized true copies of director passports, the certificate of incorporation, and the BC corporate registry search. Remote opening is permissible with an enhanced evidence package, yet a physical visit materially shortens approval timelines. The BC registered office and records office addresses must be verifiable and non-post-office-box.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial ownership combined with the unlimited-liability hybrid structure of a BC ULC, which may be electively treated as a disregarded entity or partnership for U.S. federal tax purposes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation and Articles of the ULC; BC Corporate Registry (BC Online) search confirming good standing; register of beneficial owners filed under the BC Business Corporations Act transparency amendments; organizational chart to ultimate natural persons; U.S. IRS Form 8832 check-the-box election (if any); notarized passports of directors and 25%+ shareholders; bank and professional reference letters; corporate resolution authorizing account opening; legal-tax opinion explaining the bona fide commercial purpose of the ULC and the subsection 84(2) deemed-dividend exposure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Software-as-a-Service revenue routed through Stripe and Apple In-App Purchase, a pattern that can superficially resemble money-services, payment-aggregator, or money-laundering typologies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed merchant service agreements with Stripe and Apple; platform payout and settlement statements for the most recent six months; flow-of-funds diagram proving the ULC is the sole merchant of record with no third-party pass-through; PCI DSS Attestation of Compliance (SAQ-A) for the cloud application; completed FINTRAC MSB self-assessment demonstrating the statutory exemption for persons who only process payments for their own goods or services.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No physical operating premise; reliance solely on a BC registered-office address, triggering shell-company or brass-plaque red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered-office service agreement with a licensed BC corporate-services provider; records-office address confirmation; software development and cloud-hosting contracts (e.g., AWS or Azure) evidencing substantive infrastructure; contractor or employment agreements for technical staff; detailed business plan, financial projections, and ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210 revenue model describing the personal-wealth analytics cloud product.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital-escrow deposits and subsequent rapid outbound disbursements to foreign technology subcontractors, a pattern associated with invoice fraud or trade-based money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share subscription agreements with fully subscribed share certificates; directors' resolution allocating the escrow; source-of-wealth documentation (foreign bank statements, tax filings); executed development agreements with itemized milestones; outbound invoice-to-wire mapping; Part XIII withholding analysis for royalties or management fees; internal treasury policy delineating dual approval of all disbursements.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound equity injection is executed via SWIFT MT103 wire from the foreign shareholder's bank to the ULC's Schedule I Canadian bank account. The wire must identify the beneficiary as the exact legal name of the BC ULC, include the account number, and reference the share-subscription agreement in the remittance field. The Canadian bank will require a board resolution authorizing the share issuance, the executed subscription agreement, paid-up-capital schedule, and source-of-funds attestation before the capital-escrow funds are released to the operational account. EFT reports are filed by the bank with FINTRAC for each wire at or above CAD 10,000. Subsection 84(2) planning must precede any subsequent return-of-capital, share-repurchase, or dissolution distribution to avoid deemed-dividend recharacterization with non-resident withholding implications.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary outbound rail for ISIC 6201 trade settlements is SWIFT MT103 for outsourcing of software development, cloud-infrastructure invoices, licensing royalties, and subcontractor payments; these are processed on an open-account basis with invoice-to-wire reconciliation maintained in the treasury system. For high-value hardware or master software-procurement contracts, a commercial letter of credit (LC) governed by UCP600 may be issued by the Schedule I bank with the foreign supplier as beneficiary, though in the software sector the MT103 open-account modality is market standard. All outbound wires must be mapped to an underlying invoice and contract; payments characterized as royalties, management fees, or deemed dividends to non-residents require Part XIII withholding and either a treaty-rate application or CJK-protocol exemption. CAD 10,000+ outbound EFTS are automatically reported to FINTRAC.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla OTC FX forwards (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, CAD/GBP) executed under an ISDA Master Agreement or Canadian FX master forward template
European-style FX call and put options with a Canadian chartered bank counterparty
Window and averaging-rate forwards aligned to monthly Stripe and Apple IAP settlement cycles
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CAD/USD) for long-term intercompany debt and treasury-balance conversion
FX spot-hedging via multi-currency accounts maintained with the Schedule I bank

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are legally permissible under Canadian law but commercially unnecessary for CAD, a fully convertible G10 currency; banks may price NDFs only in reduced-liquidity conditions or as a credit-constrained fallback

Separately, OSFI margin rules for non-centrally-cleared derivatives apply to financial counterparties; the ULC as a non-financial end-user is exempt from mandatory clearing and initial-margin posting, provided ISDA documentation includes the appropriate end-user exemption annex

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report under s. 272 of the Business Corporations Act (S.B.C. 2002, c. 57), including the transparency register confirmation declaration; online filing through BC Corporate Online
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registry Services, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia (Registrar of Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 months after the anniversary of the ULC's incorporation or, if an annual report was previously delivered, within 2 months after the date of the most recent annual report (the 'annual reference date'); the online filing window opens 30 days before the reference date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fee CAD 100 (approx. USD 75) for reports filed within 60 days of the due date and CAD 500 (approx. USD 375) for reports filed more than 60 days late (BC BCA ss. 273(2)-(3)); if the ULC fails to deliver annual reports for two consecutive years, the Registrar may administratively strike it off the register and dissolve it without further notice (BC BCA ss. 421-423), requiring a court restoration to resume business

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal, including BC provincial income tax administered by the CRA), with accompanying financial statements and applicable corporate schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Surrey Tax Centre / CRA My Business Account
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 6 months after the end of the ULC's taxation year (ITA s. 150(1)); balance-due date is 2 months after the year-end (3 months for an eligible Canadian-controlled private corporation), with quarterly instalments required where current-year tax payable exceeds CAD 3,000
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty under ITA s. 162(1) of 5% of the unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months; on a second failure within 3 years, 10% plus 2% per month up to 20 months; daily compound interest at the prescribed statutory rate; CRA may issue a formal demand to file, hold directors liable under failure-to-remit rules, and initiate administrative collection measures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Return (GST34-1 annual filing for small suppliers; otherwise, quarterly or monthly cycles assigned by the CRA once taxable supplies exceed the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filers: within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; quarterly filers: within 1 month after the calendar quarter-end; monthly filers: within 1 month after the month-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 1% of the unreported net tax plus 0.25% per complete month (capped at 4%), together with compound interest at the prescribed rate; continued failure allows the CRA to issue demand letters, register an Interest and Penalty Notice, and garnish or set off amounts against GST/HST credits payable

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under BC BCA s. 201, an independent auditor must be appointed at the annual general meeting unless the ULC has five or fewer shareholders and all shareholders unanimously waive the audit; a shareholder or group holding at least 1% of the issued shares may require an audit by requisition; an audit is also compulsory where the company is a public reporting issuer or where shareholders pass a special resolution requiring one
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP per the CPA Canada Handbook: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; ASPE (Handbook Part II) is available to a private BC ULC, but IFRS or US-GAAP-bridging statements are often required by the US parent for consolidated reporting

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A BC ULC must continuously maintain a transparency register of significant individuals (registered or beneficial holders or controllers of 25% or more of the shares or voting rights, or persons with 'control in fact') under BC BCA s. 119.1; every share transfer must be approved by the directors and recorded in the central securities register, and the transparency register must be updated as soon as practicable whenever a person becomes or ceases to be a significant individual; the annual report declaration to the Registrar confirms that the transparency register is complete and accurate, and the register itself is kept at the BC records office and is inspectable by shareholders and by law-enforcement or tax authorities acting under statutory authority
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (shareholder and director meeting minutes and unanimous resolutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approx. USD 260–670 (CAD 350–900) per year for a registered records-office address and corporate agent in Vancouver, British Columbia
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approx. USD 5,500–15,000 (CAD 7,500–20,000) for a full certified audit of a small fintech software entity; USD 0 where the unanimous audit waiver applies, or approx. USD 1,500–3,700 (CAD 2,000–5,000) for a review engagement

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Combined federal-provincial headline general corporate rate in British Columbia: 27% (federal 15% net of general tax reduction + BC 12%). For a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) earning active business income up to C$500,000: 11% combined (federal 9% + BC 2%). An unlimited liability corporation (BC ULC) is taxable as a corporation under the Income Tax Act (Canada) and BC Income Tax Act; it is not a domestic pass-through entity.
